items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. Filed facts all hold: בָּנִים֙ (oshb:Isa.1.2, token 8 of 13, byte tier) against בָּנִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 9 of 19, byte tier) differ only in cantillation and cross-collate at accent_stripped tier; the token-exact bare-plural object stands at 8 verses book-wide (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact) while the contiguous-substring object returns 14 (sweep: 14 verses, skeleton substring); ה֣וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.1.4 (token 1, byte tier); and the summons splice שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ stands at oshb:Isa.1.2 tokens 1-4 (byte tier). The omission is textually real: strongest_rejected_alternative rejects the merger from the near-side imperatives plus an asserted speech-move distinctness, cites no far-side bytes (the hoy onset enters the row only as an unspliced web:Isa.1.4 mention in boundary_rationale, and oshb:Isa.1.4 is absent from boundary_evidence_refs), and never weighs the catchword that the row's own device_notes disclose across the closing 1:3|1:4 seam. The finding is equally right that the seam is not unseated: the cross-seam disclosure obligation is met in device_notes, the far-side hoy onset is a ruled tier-1 signal standing in 1:4's own bytes, and on re-read no tier-4 signal serves as driver or corroboration anywhere in the row. Defective rival-rejection warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes. oshb:Isa.1.24 carries 12 tokens: נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת stands at tokens 2-5 (byte tier), after the connective לָכֵ֗ן (token 1, byte tier) and ahead of אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (tokens 6-7, byte tier). The signature census re-sweeps at 23 verses book-wide (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton) with exactly one verse-initial site, oshb:Isa.56.8 (token-exact first-token check over all 23), so the 1:24 occurrence is postpositive exactly as the row's device_notes record. The inclusio digits hold too: קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.21, tokens 4-5, byte tier) against קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.26, tokens 12-13, byte tier) cross-collate at skeleton tier only, at 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton) - byte and accent_stripped both fail because stripping removes the 1:21 atnach (U+0591) while retaining the 1:26 verse-end meteg/silluq (U+05BD), the exact mechanism the finding names. Mark types check against the staged inventory: PE at oshb:Isa.1.23, SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.1.17 and oshb:Isa.1.20, no conflation. The defect is textually exact: the rival is built on two grounds - the tier-3 petuchah AND the tier-1 neum-formula turn - but the stated rejection weighs the bracket only against 'a single tier-3 parashah witness' and 'rests on that bracket alone', with device_notes adding 'not on the signature's position'; the rival's tier-1 component is never weighed in the comparison even though the row itself holds the position data that answers it. Span not attacked; incomplete rejection warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes. וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה opens oshb:Isa.1.26 (token 1 of 13, byte tier) and תִּפָּדֶ֑ה stands at oshb:Isa.1.27 (token 3 of 5, byte tier): the first-to-third-person shift claim is byte-true, and strongest_rejected_alternative concedes the 26|27 seam 'is argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame marker'. One correction to the finding's grounds: the third-person verb IS spliced in the row - צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, tokens 1-3, byte tier) opens boundary_rationale - so 'neither form is spliced anywhere in the row' overstates. The defect nonetheless stands as filed: that splice is presented as the row's opening quotation, never as the pointed ground of the person claim; the shift's first-person pole is spliced nowhere in any field of the row (re-checked across the full row text); the seam's label is carried by the English rendering of 1:24-26; and the only pointed cross-seam evidence the row offers is the righteousness catchword it honestly reports as pulling toward continuity. Under the engagement-class law - pointed splices with tiers mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, form-class labels under digit discipline - a sole-driver mode-shift seam with its contrast pair unspliced is a defective warrant, and the row's medium_low confidence with the frontier flag is the honest calibration of exactly that gap. Medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes. The mark claim checks: the staged inventory records PE at oshb:Isa.2.4 (type correct, single-witness disclosed in the row, not conflated with the SAMEKH recorded at oshb:Isa.2.11). The tier-1 signal the finding names is real and verse-initial: בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה stands at oshb:Isa.2.5 tokens 1-4 (byte tier), and oshb:Isa.2.5 is indeed absent from boundary_evidence_refs. One precision correction: the finding's quotation truncates the because-clause, which continues 'and verse 5's imperative opens a fresh address rather than continuing the oracle's own eschatological description' - the rejection is compound, not mark-only. That does not cure the defect: the petuchah is the leading warrant in both boundary_rationale and the rejection; the imperative enters only as unspliced English with no oshb ref; and device_notes defeats the row's own disclosed house-of-Jacob bracket rival by the mark alone ('preferred here as the stronger, more local disclosure signal') - a decider role the owner addendum denies the Prophets parashah layer (tier-3 weak corroboration, never a boundary driver). The seam itself is not shown wrong - the neighbour row argues the same seam from the 2:5 bytes - so this is a warrant defect, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes. The chain is byte-true at all four cited sites and straddles this row's own closing seam: וַיִּשְׁפַּל (oshb:Isa.2.9, token 3, byte tier - accentless in the staged bytes), וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11, token 5, byte tier), וְשָׁפֵֽל (oshb:Isa.2.12, token 12, byte tier), וְשַׁח֙ (oshb:Isa.2.17, token 1, byte tier). The incoherence is textually exact: the neighbour row that owns 2:11|2:12 as its opening concedes in its device_notes a live unstated rival - one sustained pride-and-humbling poem running 2:9 through 2:17 with the refrain as internal punctuation rather than a row-cutting seam - while this row, owning the same seam as its close, files the identical device as stanza texture and confines strongest_rejected_alternative to the 2:5-22 whole-complex rival plus the flight-from-terror motif, never naming the 2:9-2:17 reading. Under cross-seam cohesion law a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disposed of; texture disclosure without disposal, opposite a neighbour that concedes the rival is live, leaves one shared seam argued incompatibly by its two owners. The seam keeps real support - the closing refrain clause is byte-identical at both stanza closes (sweep: 2 verses, byte) and a SAMEKH is recorded at oshb:Isa.2.11 (single-witness, tier-3) - so this is a rival-disclosure coherence gap, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Re-swept with the object named first. The LOW-root consonantal-substring object שפל alone accounts for the row's digit: exactly 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton substring - Isa.2.9, 2.11, 2.12, 2.17, 5.15, 10.33, 29.4, 32.19, 40.4, 57.15), and every one of the four chain sites is inside it because each also carries a LOW-root form. The BOW member וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11, token 5, byte tier) is a different count object with different digits, none of them 10: byte 1 verse; accent_stripped 2 verses (2.11, 2.17); token-exact skeleton 2 verses; contiguous-substring skeleton 4 verses (2.11, 2.17, 22.13, 45.8); and the bare two-letter skeleton שח runs to 40 verses (sweep: 40 verses, skeleton substring) - the short-token trap the hazard catalog names. The shipped sentence defines the chain across both roots, attaches the single digit 10, and never names the swept object; semantic-class count discipline requires the object named before the digit and bars blended sweeps, so the defect is real exactly as filed. Per the orchestrator reconciliation_note this is a severity item only. Texture-level digit defect in device_notes, not load-bearing for the boundary: medium as filed.

Re-collated. The maximal byte-identical run shared by oshb:Isa.2.11 and oshb:Isa.2.17 is the seven-token tail ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא (byte tier at both sites; sweep: 2 verses, byte), not the five-token clause alone (itself byte tier at the same 2 verses): extending one token leftward breaks byte identity in both directions - וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11, token 5, byte tier) against וְשָׁפֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.2.17, token 4, byte tier) differ at byte and even skeleton tier, and each eight-token extension sweeps to exactly 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, byte, from either side). The two extra shared tokens ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים (byte tier at both sites) are loftiness-of-man material, while the word-order variation the same shipped sentence asserts is real only in the clause head - גַּבְה֤וּת אָדָם֙ (oshb:Isa.2.11, tokens 2-3, byte tier) against גַּבְה֣וּת הָאָדָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.2.17, tokens 2-3, byte tier) fail even accent_stripped collation. The shipped sentence restricting byte-identity to the closing clause alone is therefore byte-false as written, exactly as filed. It sits in device_notes qualifying the refrain bracket; the load-bearing identity claim - the refrain clause byte-identical at both stanza closes - survives and is strengthened rather than weakened. Byte-false but not load-bearing: medium as filed.
